title: Palindrome Linked List
prompt:
Write a `ListNode` class and an `isPalindrome` function in `solution.ts`:

**Requirements:**
1. `ListNode` class with `val: number` and `next: ListNode | null` properties, and a constructor `constructor(val = 0, next: ListNode | null = null)`
2. `isPalindrome(head)` -- returns `true` if the linked list reads the same forwards and backwards, `false` otherwise. Solve in O(n) time and O(1) space by reversing the second half in-place

**Algorithm:**
1. Find the middle node using slow/fast pointers
2. Reverse the second half of the list starting from `slow`
3. Compare the first half and the reversed second half node by node
4. If all values match, return `true`. Otherwise return `false`

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(1) space.

**Examples:**
```typescript
// [1, 2, 2, 1] -> true
// [1, 2] -> false
// [1] -> true
// [1, 2, 3, 2, 1] -> true
```
hints: Find the middle with slow/fast pointers -- slow ends at the start of the second half
Reverse the second half in-place using the standard three-pointer technique
Compare the first half (starting at head) with the reversed second half (starting at prev)
Only compare while right is not null -- the reversed half may be shorter for odd-length lists

solution.ts.name: isPalindrome
solution.ts.description: Define isPalindrome that accepts a head node
Use while loops for finding the middle, reversing, and comparing
solution.ts.hint: You need at least two while loops: one for slow/fast traversal and one for reversal
